The congruence–bias parameterisation

Source: vignettes/articles/reparameterisation.Rmd
reparameterisation.Rmd

The widget below demonstrates the recommended congruence–bias parameterisation by simulating ten pairs of counts from a model (see rbicount()). The relationship with the native parameterisation is shown by moving the sliders: a change to a parameter in one parameterisation changes the parameters in the other. The plot below the sliders shows the expected decomposition of the two counts (left) and the simulated pairs (right).

Congruence–bias parameterisation

Native parameterisation

The coordinates of the congruence–bias parameterisation directly represent the quantities usually of interest in a comparison of two sources:

Coordinate Meaning Definition Name in brms
M midpoint of the expected counts of the two sources M = \mu + (\lambda_1 + \lambda_2)/2 logM, for \log M
f congruence, the proportion of M recorded by both sources f = \mu / M logitf, for \operatorname{logit} f
\beta source bias, zero when the two exclusive rates are equal \beta = (\lambda_1 - \lambda_2)/(\lambda_1 + \lambda_2) delta, for \operatorname{artanh}\beta
\kappa_s, \kappa_{x1}, \kappa_{x2} overdispersions \kappa = 1/\sqrt{\phi} kappas, kappaxone, kappaxtwo

The native parameters are the rates and dispersions of the three latent components:

Parameter Meaning Definition Name in brms
\mu rate of the shared component, recorded by both sources \mu = Mf mu
\lambda_1 rate of the source-exclusive component of source 1 \lambda_1 = M(1 - f)(1 + \beta) lambdaone
\lambda_2 rate of the source-exclusive component of source 2 \lambda_2 = M(1 - f)(1 - \beta) lambdatwo
\phi_s, \phi_{x1}, \phi_{x2} NB2 (inverse) dispersions \phi = 1/\kappa^2 shapes, shapexone, shapextwo

The functions mfd_to_dpars() and dpars_to_mfd() convert between the two parameterisations, for single values or for vectors of posterior draws:

library(bicountbrms)

dpars <- mfd_to_dpars(
  M      = 12,
  f      = 0.67,
  delta  = atanh(0.2),
  kappas = 0.6,
  kappax = 1.0
)
unlist(dpars)
#>        mu lambdaone lambdatwo    shapes shapexone shapextwo 
#>  8.040000  4.752000  3.168000  2.777778  1.000000  1.000000

mfd <- dpars_to_mfd(
  mu        = dpars$mu,
  lambdaone = dpars$lambdaone,
  lambdatwo = dpars$lambdatwo
)
unlist(mfd[c("M", "f", "beta")])
#>     M     f  beta 
#> 12.00  0.67  0.20
